understanding: WISHBONE top sequence on wishbone_slave_interface_agent drives controlled register reads and writes within documented addresses 0-6 with DLAB gating, reusing init DLAB base; clock fixed per test, coverage sampled on completion.
preconditions: Chip reset completed with FIFOs cleared and reset values applied [f_reset_div_zero] [f_reset_lcr_8n1] [f_reset_ier_disabled], clock period fixed per test before traffic
init_config_sequence completed with MSB-first divisor programming then DLAB cleared to 0 for normal-register handoff [f_div_order_msb_first] [f_dlab_disable_access] [f_dlab_enable_access]
wishbone_slave_interface_agent owns DUT inputs wb_adr_i wb_dat_i wb_we_i wb_stb_i wb_cyc_i and observes wb_dat_o wb_ack_o on clock edges; bus idle before start
stimulus_steps: WAIT for init handoff with tracked DLAB=0 and wishbone bus idle

FOR each directed bring-up slot in documented order: drive one access via wishbone_slave_interface_agent only using wb_adr_i for pin address value, wb_we_i for documented direction, wb_dat_i for symbolic write byte; WAIT for wb_ack_o completion on observed clock edges before next start [f_rbr_addr0] [f_thr_addr0] [f_ier_addr1] [f_iir_fcr_addr2] [f_lcr_addr3] [f_mcr_lsr_msr_addr456]

IF tracked DLAB==0 THEN constrain addr to 0 to 6 normal mapping with documented R/W/RW per address [f_rbr_addr0] [f_thr_addr0] [f_ier_addr1] [f_iir_fcr_addr2] [f_lcr_addr3] [f_mcr_lsr_msr_addr456]; ELSE IF tracked DLAB==1 THEN constrain addr to 0 divisor LSB and 1 divisor MSB RW only [f_dll_lsb] [f_dlm_msb] [f_dlab_gate_divisor] [f_dlab_gate_normal_blocked]

FOR N controlled transactions under reproducible seed with volume and idle knobs as testbench operational limits: randomize symbolic addr, symbolic data byte class, and read-vs-write within documented access types and current DLAB gating; update tracked DLAB on LCR bit7 writes respecting MSB-first then LSB-next divisor order [f_div_order_msb_first] [f_dlab_enable_access] [f_dlab_disable_access]; drive back-to-back or idle gaps without changing clock period

On LCR write changing DLAB: IF new DLAB==1 THEN next divisor accesses use addr 0 LSB and addr 1 MSB; IF new DLAB==0 THEN return to normal 0-6 mapping [f_dlab_gate_divisor] [f_dlab_gate_normal_blocked] [f_dll_lsb] [f_dlm_msb]
Cleanup: drive LCR write to clear DLAB to 0, WAIT for completion, leave wishbone bus idle-owned for traffic handoff [f_dlab_disable_access]
coverage_steps: SAMPLE cg_wb_reg_access for addr 0-6 with read/write direction and byte data class on each completion via wishbone monitor analysis port [f_ier_addr1] [f_mcr_lsr_msr_addr456]

SAMPLE rc_wb_regs for reg0 RBR vs THR, reg1 IER, reg2 IIR vs FCR, reg3 LCR, reg4 MCR, reg5 LSR, reg6 MSR with addr7 illegal and DLAB-mismatch ignore via monitor [f_rbr_addr0] [f_thr_addr0] [f_ier_addr1] [f_iir_fcr_addr2] [f_lcr_addr3]
SAMPLE cg_cross_addr_dlab for addr0/addr1 alias vs addr2-6 normal crossed with DLAB on each completion via monitor [f_dlab_gate_divisor] [f_dlab_gate_normal_blocked] [f_dll_lsb] [f_dlm_msb]
SAMPLE cg_dlab_divisor for DLAB state with LSB and MSB byte values including zero and maximum on divisor completions via monitor [f_dll_lsb] [f_dlm_msb]
completion: Done when directed slots plus N controlled transactions all completed with monitor-sampled coverage and DLAB=0 idle cleanup
Bound by TEST_TIMEOUT_CYCLES operational limit; timeout is testbench limit not DUT timing

facts.statement: Receiver Buffer at WISHBONE address 0 is 8-bit read-only Receiver FIFO output.
facts.quote: Receiver Buffer 0 8 R Receiver FIFO output

facts.statement: Transmitter Holding Register at WISHBONE address 0 is 8-bit write-only Transmit FIFO input.
Divisor latch registers are accessible when LCR bit 7 DLAB is set to 1.
facts.quote: The registers can be accessed when the 7th (DLAB) bit of the Line Control Register is set

facts.statement: Normal registers at addresses 0-1 cannot be accessed when LCR bit 7 DLAB is set to 1.
facts.quote: At this time the above registers at addresses 0-1 can’t be accessed.

facts.statement: Divisor Latch LSB at WISHBONE address 0 is 8-bit RW.
facts.quote: Divisor Latch Byte 1 (LSB) 0 8 RW The LSB of the divisor

facts.statement: Divisor Latch MSB at WISHBONE address 1 is 8-bit RW.
facts.quote: Divisor Latch Byte 2 1 8 RW The MSB of the divisor

facts.statement: Interrupt Enable register at WISHBONE address 1 is 8-bit RW.
At WISHBONE address 2 Interrupt Identification is read-only and FIFO Control is write-only.
facts.quote:
Interrupt Identification 2 8 R Get interrupt information
FIFO Control 2 8 W Control FIFO options

facts.statement: Line Control Register at WISHBONE address 3 is 8-bit RW for connection control.
facts.quote: Line Control Register 3 8 RW Control connection

facts.statement: Modem Control at address 4 is write-only, Line Status at address 5 is read-only, Modem Status at address 6 is read-only.
facts.quote:
Modem Control 4 8 W Controls modem
Line Status 5 8 R Status information
Modem Status 6 8 R Modem Status

facts.statement: Divisor programming order is MSB first then LSB next.
facts.quote: Set the Divisor Latches, MSB first, LSB next.

facts.statement: Setting LCR bit 7 to 1 allows access to Divisor Latches.
facts.quote:
Set bit 7 to ‘1’
to allow access to the Divisor Latches.

facts.statement: Clearing LCR bit 7 to 0 disables Divisor Latch access and returns to normal registers.
facts.quote: Set bit 7 of LCR to ‘0’ to disable access to Divisor Latches.

facts.statement: After reset Divisor Latch register is 0.
facts.quote: The Divisor Latch register is set to 0.

facts.statement: After reset LCR is 8 bits data no parity 1 stop bit.
facts.quote:
The Line Control Register is set to communication of 8 bits of data, no parity, 1
stop bit.

facts.statement: After reset all interrupts are disabled in Interrupt Enable Register.
facts.quote: All interrupts are disabled in the Interrupt Enable Register.

questions: What are documented legal masks and access types per WISHBONE address for random constraints?
What is wb_rst_i polarity and required deassert-to-first-write delay after reset before init and top traffic?
What are required wb_sel_i values, owners and tie-offs for 8-bit FIFO-only use, and inactive levels of wb_stb_i and wb_cyc_i that must be driven?
What are documented legal data values/masks per writable register (IER enables, LCR line bits, FCR trigger, MCR, THR, divisor LSB/MSB including whether divisor 0 is illegal) for constrained random?
What is explicit bus address representation for wb_adr_i pin values (3-bit vs 5-bit) and required handling of addr 7 which is illegal for 8-bit use?
